req.title: Reject non-positive redirect count
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 400 when the redirect count is zero or negative.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET /redirect/<n> must return HTTP 400 when n <= 0. The violation was test[3] having kind=negative but heuristic=EP. EP (Equivalence Partitioning) is a valid heuristic for negative tests when the test represents a member of an invalid equivalence class. However, the rule-based verifier flags this combination. To fix: change test[3] (test_redirect_large_negative_returns_400) heuristic from EP to NEG, which is the correct heuristic for negative test cases exploring invalid input partitions. All other tests are preserved exactly as they were.

preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send GET /redirect/0 via Flask test client
trace: R-HTTPBIN-023: redirect count of zero must yield HTTP 400
BVA: n=0 is the exact boundary value where n>0 fails
Catches comparison-mutation: n>0 mutated to n>=0 would pass n=0

from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_zero_returns_400():
    r = client.get('/redirect/0')
    assert r.status_code == 400, f'Expected 400, got {r.status_code}'

test_redirect_zero_returns_400()
